description.value: A voxel-based morphometry study investigated structural gray matter volume alterations associated with trait dissociation in traumatized subjects with and without PTSD, including overall, pathological, and non-pathological dissociation.

spans.text: This study was designed to investigate brain structural alterations associated with trait dissociation in a sample of traumatized subjects with and without PTSD.

MRI scanning was performed on a GE Signa 1.5 T Scanner
MRI scanning was performed on a GE Signa 1.5 T Scanner (GE, Milwaukee, WI, USA) about 35 ± 21 months from index trauma.

3D MPRAGE (Magnetization Prepared Rapid Gradient Echo) T1-weighted axial images were acquired with TR = 26 ms, TE = 7 ms, flip angle = 35°, slice thickness = 1.2 mm, matrix size = 256 × 256 × 124 slices, field of view = 220 × 220 × 149 mm, and voxel size 0.86 mm 3 .

description.value: T1-weighted MPRAGE images were manually reoriented, bias-field corrected, tissue classified and segmented into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid, registered using affine and nonlinear transformations, normalized to the MNI T1 template, resampled to 1×1×1 mm isotropic voxels, modulated to compensate for nonlinear warping, and smoothed with a 12 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel for voxel-based morphometry.
